title: Introduction to cobud
text: want two years, can just add years param. important limitation LCS forecast JBC forecast cover two future years. years beyond , param use “LCS forecast” “JBC forecast” methods. “LCS forecast” heavily used templates, want forecast two years, need specify lots assumptions. One simple options take anything forecasted instead grow inflation FY 2028-29.
code: # start with the param template three_year_params = very_simple_param_template  # copy the 26-27 params twice three_year_params[["27-28"]] = three_year_params[["26-27"]] three_year_params[["28-29"]] = three_year_params[["26-27"]]  # try to run the forecast  try(   cobud_forecast(three_year_params) ) #> Error in validate_revenue_forecasts(params, rev, spend) :  #>   validate_revenue_forecasts error: year '28-29' field 'inflation_pct' uses method 'LCS forecast' but revenue_forecast has no non-missing value for that field and year  # observe that "LCS forecast" was invoked but no forecast data was provided three_year_params[["28-29"]][["inflation_pct"]] #> $method #> [1] "LCS forecast" cobud_revenue_forecast |> select(year, inflation_pct) #>    year inflation_pct #> 1 26-27         0.025 #> 2 27-28         0.031 # set a custom inflation assumption three_year_params[["28-29"]][["inflation_pct"]] = list(   method = "Custom",   value = 0.042 # 4.2% inflation )  # change any "LCS forecast" or "JBC forecast" uses to "Inflation"  use_inf <- function(x) {   if("LCS forecast" %in% x$method | "JBC forecast" %in% x$method) {     x$method = "Inflation"   }    return(x) } three_year_params[["28-29"]] = lapply(three_year_params[["28-29"]], use_inf)  # tweak a few options that rely on the LCS forecast three_year_params[["28-29"]]$options$`scale diversions with income tax` = FALSE three_year_params[["28-29"]]$options$`scale exempt portion of other revenue` = FALSE  # run the three year forecast three_year_forecast = cobud_forecast(three_year_params) #> inputs validated #> preparing tax credit triggers... #>    for 25-26 ... #>    for 26-27 ... #>    for 27-28 ... #>    for 28-29 ... #> calculating 25-26 budget... #>    using very simple appropriations... #> calculating 26-27 budget... #>    using very simple appropriations... #> calculating 27-28 budget... #>    using very simple appropriations... #> calculating 28-29 budget... #>    using very simple appropriations... #> budget calculation successful #> outputs validated three_year_forecast |>   select(year, sales_tax, gf_end_balance) #>     year sales_tax gf_end_balance #> 1  15-16  2585.300       512.7000 #> 2  16-17  2727.700       614.5000 #> 3  17-18  2926.000      1366.0000 #> 4  18-19  3054.000      1262.6000 #> 5  19-20  3196.000      1825.7000 #> 6  20-21  3418.100      3181.5000 #> 7  21-22  4089.000      3203.2000 #> 8  22-23  4301.600      2427.4000 #> 9  23-24  4362.600      3153.5000 #> 10 24-25  4441.100      2408.4000 #> 11 25-26  4600.100      2045.7950 #> 12 26-27  4798.500      1113.1521 #> 13 27-28  5046.000      -103.8884 #> 14 28-29   211.932    -19095.7767

Custom assumptions can supplied varying levels detail, single total appropriations figure department-level detail, can optionally draw outside revenue spending forecasts. Historical data, forecasts, assumption templates maintained Colorado Legislative Council Staff (LCS) economics team.

title: Forecast Colorado's General Fund budget — cobud_forecast
text: params nested list forecast assumptions, one element per fiscal year forecast, format detailed_param_template, simple_param_template, very_simple_param_template. Years must consecutive may include final year historical_data (current, -progress year) plus number future years. historical_data data frame historical budget data format cobud_history. Defaults package's cobud_history data. revenue_forecast optional data frame forecasted revenue TABOR fields format cobud_revenue_forecast. Required element params uses "LCS forecast" calculation method revenue field. Defaults package's cobud_revenue_forecast data. spending_forecast optional data frame forecasted spending fields format cobud_spending_forecast. Required element params uses "JBC forecast" calculation method spending field. Defaults package's cobud_spending_forecast data.
